title: MS NOW Hosts ‘Disappointed’ Management Has Yet to Reach New WGA Union Deal Guaranteeing ‘Fair Wages’; Network Boss Rebecca Kutler Responds to Accusations
full_text: × Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Nov 24, 2026 10:56am PT MS NOW Hosts ‘Disappointed’ Management Has Yet to Reach New WGA Union Deal Guaranteeing ‘Fair Wages’; Network Boss Rebecca Kutler Responds to Accusations By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest MS NOW Hosts ‘Disappointed’ Management Has Yet to Reach New WGA Union Deal Guaranteeing ‘Fair Wages’; Network Boss Rebecca Kutler Responds to Accusations 48 minutes ago Trump Posts Bizarre AI Meme of Jensen Huang Holding Up a Bra, Riffing Off 2024 Assassination Attempt on President, After Nvidia Board Reinstates CEO 1 day ago Byron Allen’s BuzzFeed Hires Chris Poydenis, Co-Founder of Creator Marketing Agency Influential, as Chief Revenue Officer 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images (Rachel Maddow); Courtesy of MS NOW (Rebecca Kutler) Rachel Maddow and more than a dozen other MS NOW on-air hosts issued a public letter urging parent company Versant Media to reach a new deal with unionized employees affiliated with WGA East that ensures “fair wages and protections,” before their previous agreement expires Dec. 3. Rebecca Kutler , MS NOW’s president, responded to their complaints in a memo to the outlet’s staffers — writing in part, “We must weigh every financial commitment against our ability to invest in journalism.” Related Stories ‘PAW Patrol’ Spinoff Series ‘Skye’s Pup Squad’ Set for 2027 Release Writers Guild of America East members at MS NOW are currently negotiating for a second collective bargaining agreement. “Despite the network’s historic midterm ratings and strong performance across the business, workers are still fighting for a fair contract with Versant Media Group management,” the union said. MS NOW hosts and guests including Rachel Maddow, Jen Psaki, Christopher Hayes, Lawrence O’Donnell and Nicolle Wallace signed onto “a letter of solidarity calling for a fair wages and protections for the MS NOW Union,” released Tuesday by WGA East. Others signing the letter included Ali Velshi, Amy McGrath, Alicia Menendez, Jacob Soboroff, David Noriega, Jillian Frankel, Ayman Mohyeldin, Katie Phang, Christine Jansing, Symone Sanders Townsend, Antonia Hylton, Jonathan Capehart and Michael Steele. (The signatories to the letter are not covered by the WGAE agreement.) The letter, which WGA East said was delivered to Versant management at the bargaining table, reads: “As hosts and guests of MS NOW programs, we stand in solidarity with the MS NOW Union as they fight for a contract that addresses inflation, AI protections and retirement security. As one of the most trusted names in news, we are proud of our programming and the MS NOW producers that make it possible. We’re disappointed that Versant Media’s decision makers expect unit members to work extra hours creating new digital content, without treating it as extra work or paying for it. On top of that, we are disappointed that Versant Media will not agree to the Union’s demands for annual and minimum wage increases that keep pace with inflation. We are calling on the company to agree to a quick and fair process to recognize all employees’ rightful place in the MS NOW Union without division or delay. Additionally, we call on the company to agree to a contract that will protect wages, benefits and security at work.” Kutler, who has led MS NOW since January 2025, addressed many of the allegations in a memo. “Let me be clear: we support our employees’ right to organize, to be represented, and to advocate for themselves. That has never been in question, nor should it be,” she wrote. According to Kutler, MS NOW has already reached “tentative agreements” with WGAE on “numerous issues throughout this process and shown a willingness to find common ground where differences remain.” “We have made meaningful proposals to increase compensation, address workload concerns, expand opportunities for growth and advancement, and provide protections against AI, among many other offerings,” Kutler said. That said, according to Kutler, MS NOW’s success “does not insulate us from the financial pressures reshaping our industry. It takes a realistic understanding of these market pressures for us to continue our success. We must weigh every financial commitment against our ability to invest in journalism, develop new programming, hire journalists, cover the 2028 presidential campaign, and build out platforms that will carry MS NOW into the future, including our direct-to-consumer offering.” Kutler said MS NOW will “continue to compensate our employees fairly and competitively, while protecting our long-term growth. Those responsibilities are not mutually exclusive, but they require thoughtful decisions.” “As we approach the final weeks of these negotiations, let’s stay focused on what unites us: our shared commitment to the journalism we produce, the audiences who count on us, and the future of MS NOW. I am optimistic that together we will reach a fair and responsible agreement that reflects the respect we have for our colleagues and the work we do together,” Kutler said. In addition to guarantees on wages and overtime pay for MS NOW union workers, the WGAE is seeking to expand union jurisdiction at MS NOW during negotiations for the unit’s second union contract. The currently 300-member bargaining unit is demanding union recognition for approximately 50 additional workers including employees in MS NOW’s digital, audio and longform, newsgathering, planning and DC bureau divisions. The union’s first contract, ratified as the MSNBC Union in 2023, included a minimum 3% pay increase every year for the three-year contract’s duration and improvements to policies regarding extra pay for additional work, overnight work and out-of-title work. MS NOW changed its name from MSNBC in the fall of 2025 , ahead of its spin-off as part of Versant from NBCUniversal at the beginning of this year. In the past year, Kutler noted in her memo Tuesday, MS NOW reached new collective bargaining agreements with other labor organizations, including two International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees locals and the Directors Guild of America. According to Kutler, MS NOW offers the highest starting salaries among its peers, “having raised entry-level salaries significantly over the last five years, and the starting point for each role’s salary range is typically higher than our broadcast and cable news competitors.” In addition, according to Kutler, “while many other news organizations are cutting back their newsrooms and trimming roles, we have filled more than 200 in the past year at MS NOW and continue recruiting for dozens of open positions.” ‘Friends’ Cast Entered Matthew Perry’s Funeral Holding Hands and Cried Around the Casket, Netflix Documentary Reveals David Schwimmer Reunites With His Famous Red Sweater From ‘Friends’ in Nostalgic Quince Campaign Loading comments...

MS NOW has been building its newsgathering operation since the split from Comcast meant that NBC News was no longer a sister network. The first contract for the MS NOW Union [previously MSNBC] was reached in 2023 and included a 3% pay increase for every year of the agreement’s duration. It also included “vital improvements to policies regarding extra pay for additional work, overnight work, and out-of-title work,” per the WGAE. According to the network, they have offered guaranteed 3% salary increases, enhanced pay for filling in at an upgraded position, and a 33% increase in the night shift allowance per shift for exempt employees, crediting on-call time as time worked, as well as AI-related protections, among other proposals. Per the network, WGAE is seeking 5% annual wage increases over the next two years and a 4.5% increase in the third year, as well as a 4% increase in salary minimums at signing and another 4.5% increase in 2029. Kutler wrote that the network’s audience growth “does not insulate us from the financial pressures reshaping our industry. It takes a realistic understanding of these market pressures for us to continue our success.” The letters from the WGAE and Kutler are below: The WGAE letter: As hosts and guests of MS NOW programs, we stand in solidarity with the MS NOW Union as they fight for a contract that addresses inflation, AI protections, and retirement security. As one of the most trusted names in news, we are proud of our programming and the MS NOW producers that make it possible. We’re disappointed that Versant Media’s decision makers expect unit members to work extra hours creating new digital content, without treating it as extra work or paying for it. Kutler’s memo: Team, As we continue to negotiate with the Writers Guild of America East, I’d like to give you an update about where we stand. For those unfamiliar with this process, the WGAE represents a group of our editorial employees in a collective bargaining unit that negotiates their compensation and other terms of employment. We reached an initial agreement with this union in 2023, and now that contract is set to expire on Dec. 3. Let me be clear: we support our employees’ right to organize, to be represented, and to advocate for themselves. That has never been in question, nor should it be. In the past year, we have successfully reached new collective bargaining agreements with other labor organizations, including two International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees locals and the Directors Guild of America, and have approached these negotiations with the same mindset. We have already reached tentative agreements with WGAE on numerous issues throughout this process and shown a willingness to find common ground where differences remain. We have made meaningful proposals to increase compensation, address workload concerns, expand opportunities for growth and advancement, and provide protections against AI, among many other offerings. We offer the highest starting salaries among our peers, having raised entry-level salaries significantly over the last five years, and the starting point for each role’s salary range is typically higher than our broadcast and cable news competitors. We are a workforce that is embracing new technologies and creating opportunities for employees to broaden their skill sets and advance their careers. Our goal is to ensure our employees will grow alongside our business and the broader industry. These commitments are part of the reason we have a company-wide attrition rate well below national averages. Plus, while many other news organizations are cutting back their newsrooms and trimming roles, we have filled more than 200 in the past year at MS NOW and continue recruiting for dozens of open positions. We are enormously proud of MS NOW’s performance; our strong audience metrics are a testament to the work you do every day. But this success does not insulate us from the financial pressures reshaping our industry. It takes a realistic understanding of these market pressures for us to continue our success. We must weigh every financial commitment against our ability to invest in journalism, develop new programming, hire journalists, cover the 2028 presidential campaign, and build out platforms that will carry MS NOW into the future, including our direct-to-consumer offering. We will continue to compensate our employees fairly and competitively, while protecting our long-term growth. Those responsibilities are not mutually exclusive, but they require thoughtful decisions. As we approach the final weeks of these negotiations, let’s stay focused on what unites us: our shared commitment to the journalism we produce, the audiences who count on us, and the future of MS NOW. I am optimistic that together we will reach a fair and responsible agreement that reflects the respect we have for our colleagues and the work we do together. If you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to reach out to me, Greg, Madeleine, Scott, Marcus, or anyone on our leadership team. Our doors are always open. title: Benjamín Naishtat’s ‘The Seven Madmen,’ With ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Selton Mello, Wraps Production
full_text: × Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Nov 24, 2026 10:31am PT Benjamín Naishtat’s ‘The Seven Madmen,’ With ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Selton Mello, Wraps Production ‘The Seven Madmen’ marks the latest from ‘Rojo’ and ‘Glaxo’ helmer Benjamín Naishtat, fast-consolidating as one of Latin America’s major directors By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest Benjamín Naishtat’s ‘The Seven Madmen,’ With ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Selton Mello, Wraps Production 1 hour ago Huelva Ibero-American Film Festival Prizes: ‘After Elena,’ Alfredo Castro, Lucía Puenzo and ‘La Bola Negra’ Win Big 2 days ago ‘Sentimental Value’ Creative Duo Joachim Trier and Eskil Vogt Set for Göteborg Fest’s Nordic Honorary Dragon Award 2027 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Martín Piroyansky, Benjamín Naishtat, Selton Mello Credits: Martín Piroyansky: Camila Fortunato; Selton Mello: courtesy of Maurício Nahas, and Benjamín Naishtat, courtesy of the San Sebastián Film Festival, photo by Nora Jauregui “ The Seven Madmen ,” starring Selton Mello (“I’m Still Here”) and directed by Benjamín Naishtat, is wrapping its shoot in Buenos Aires on Nov. 24, marking the latest advance on a production that weighs in as one of Latin America’s big bets for A-List festival selection in 2027. A present day noir thriller loosely adapting Argentinean novelist Robert Arlt’s 1929 and 1931 modern classic novels “The Seven Madmen” and “The Flamethrowers,” the movie also reps the latest feature from Argentina’s Naishtat (“Rojo,” “Puan,” “Glaxo”) who is fast consolidating as one of Latin America’s major auteurs. Related Stories ‘PAW Patrol’ Spinoff Series ‘Skye’s Pup Squad’ Set for 2027 Release Naishtat also forms part of a loose knit but burgeoning new generation of Spanish-language cineastes (think Spain’s Rodrigo Sorogoyen) that have a clear sense of film genre and combine bold visuals with a large concern for contemporary social issues. “The Seven Madmen” also stars Martin Piroyansky (“Porno y helado”). Arlt’s novel of the same time turned on young Remo Erdosian who’s threatened with imprisonment unless he returns money he’s stolen. He seeks out Alberto, a mysterious Astrologer, who promises to help Remo if in return the young man joins his organization which, he discovers, aims to overthrow the government. Just how much of that get into Naishtat’s film, given it is also inspired by “The Flamethrowers,” remains to be seen with its producers keeping its plot under wraps, describing it as “set in a twisted Buenos Aires” and “an intense thriller.” It is known, however, that Piroyansky plays Remo and Mello the Astrologer. “Benjamín is a deeply inspiring filmmaker,” Mello told Variety . “It is an honor to have been invited by him to bring to life one of the most iconic characters in Argentine literature: El Astrólogo, created by Roberto Arlt and now reimagined by Benjamín in the film we are making together.” Mello added: “I have been experiencing something new: a sense of Latin American belonging that moves me deeply while also expanding my artistic expression. This project has brought about an intimate celebration of a rare and very special moment in my journey.” Cast is rounded up by Lorena Vega (“Envious”), Diego Cremonesi, Sofía Morandi, Andrea Frigerio, Iván González, Paula Grinszpan and Lola Berthet, with Carla Peterson (“27 Nights”) and special guest star Mercedes Morán (“The Kingdom”). “Ever since I first read ‘The Seven Madmen,’ I have been captivated by its dark beauty, by its characters who exist beyond the reach of any law, and by its ability to capture Buenos Aires in a way perhaps no other book ever has,” said Naishtat. He added that he had spent “more than 10 years” working on an adaptation which he knew was “impossible, which, in a way, came as a relief, since my interpretation is decidedly free.” “At the darkest moment in Argentine cinema, devastated by a government hostile to any form of cultural expression, an eclectic group of producers from around the world, an extraordinary cast, and a world-class crew joined forces to make this project a reality.” In an era where Latin American films of late ambition can only be made with streaming service support or multi-lateral co-production, the “eclectic group” referred to by Naishtat takes in Argentina’s Púcara Cine, founded by Federico Eibuszyc, which produced Naishtat’s “The Movement,” “Rojo” and “Puán” and Pasto, founded by Bárbara Francisco Mendivilm which teamed with Púcara to produce “Puan.” They are joined by “Argentina 1985” producer Infinity Hill , Particular Crowd (“The Extortion”) and Brazilian production companies MyMama Entertainment (“Medusa”) and Bubbles Project (“Elephants in the Fog,”) and Ecce Films (France), Materia Cinema (Spain), and Pandora Films (Germany), in association with Bord Cadre and Sula Films. It is no coincidence that two novels published in 1929 and 1931, an era of social fanaticism which saw the rise of fascism, are now set to receive a free present-day adaptation. “Revisiting the unclassifiable marvel that Roberto Arlt published in 1929 is a timely endeavor in order to decipher the Argentinian and planetary present, said Naishtat. Noted Particular Crowd President Peter Bevan: ”’The Seven Madmen’ pulsates with relentless tension, singular humor and Benjamín Naishtat’s signature lucidity.” Lorena Vega David Schwimmer Reunites With His Famous Red Sweater From ‘Friends’ in Nostalgic Quince Campaign ‘Friends’ Cast Entered Matthew Perry’s Funeral Holding Hands and Cried Around the Casket, Netflix Documentary Reveals Loading comments...

title: Disney Greenlights ‘Aquamarine’ Series Inspired by the 2006 Mermaid Movie; Emma Roberts to Reprise Role and Exec Produce
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All November 24, 2026 10:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emma Roberts (left) and Kenzi Richardson Michael Buckner/WWD/Getty Images; David Muller Disney has greenlighted Aquamarine , a new live-action series inspired by the 2006 feature film. Original stars Emma Roberts and Jake McDorman are reprising their roles from the cult classic and also serving as executive producers. Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum, who directed the original movie, directs the pilot and exec produces alongside Susan Cartsonis, who produced the film. In the series, Kenzi Richardson stars as (Coral), a teenager who moves to a dreamy seaside town. There, she begins unraveling the truth behind her mother’s disappearance and discovers her mother is a mermaid, awakening magical powers in Coral just as secrets beneath the waves threaten to surface. Related Stories TV 'Only Murders in the Building' Stars Steve Martin and Martin Short, Without Selena Gomez, Cross Pond for Star-Studded Season 6 London Premiere Beyond the Book 'Percy Jackson and the Olympians': How Season 3 Brings Epic Moments to Life and Deals With Annabeth's Absence in the Books The cast also includes Briella Guiza (as Mia), Theodore Dalton (as August) and Annika Reese (as Paige). Roberts (who played Claire in the film) and McDorman (Raymond) reprise their roles from the film and serve as executive producers. “ Aquamarine is a timeless coming-of-age story, and we’re excited to bring its humor, heart and sense of wonder to a new generation,” said Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family. “At its core, it’s a story about the power of friendship, self-discovery and believing in yourself. And with a stellar cast led by Kenzi Richardson, there’s a magical quality to this story that I think audiences everywhere will really connect with.” The original film, which was loosely based on Alice Hoffman’s 2001 YA novel, followed two teenage girls, played by Roberts and Joanna “JoJo” Levesque, who discover that mermaids really do exist after a violent storm washes one ashore. The mermaid, a sassy creature named Aquamarine (Sara Paxton), is determined to prove to her father that real love exists; she also enlists the girls’ help in winning the heart of a handsome lifeguard (McDorman). The movie earned moderately positive reviews but was not a huge box office hit when it was released. However, it’s become a cult classic in the years since its release, and its fan base includes some famous faces. Addison Rae has said her song “Aquamarine” was inspired by the film, and Chappell Roan has described her music video for “Casual” as “ Aquamarine , but like gay.” Disney had ordered a pilot for the live-action series over the summer. The show is executive produced by Melissa Carter ( The Cleaning Lady) , Rosenbaum ( Purple Hearts , Guarding Stars ) and Cartsonis ( Descendants 3 ), alongside Roberts and McDorman. The pilot is written by Sarah Watson ( The Bold Type ), directed by Rosenbaum, and executive produced by Watson, Rosenbaum, Cartsonis, Roberts and McDorman. Disney said the series builds on its expanding slate of coming-of-age shows for Disney+ and Hulu that also includes Percy Jackson and the Olympians, Coven Academy and Phony . THR

title: Joe Rogan’s The Most Trusted Name In Media For Dudes – Especially Dudes With Daddy Issues
full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Joe Rogan’s The Most Trusted Name In Media For Dudes – Especially Dudes With Daddy Issues “Not True”: Antoine Fuqua Alleged Gun Assault Of Bar Manager Over Daughter Rebuked By Reps Indie Film Accountant Gets Prison For Stealing Millions For Sugar Daddy Hook-Ups, Vegas Visits & Louis Vuitton Gear View All November 24, 2026 10:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The Joe Rogan Experience podcast displayed on a phone Getty When Dolly Parton sadly passed earlier this year, the chorus of grief all agreed that the 9-to-5 singer was one of the few figures in American public life that everyone admired. Turns out that might be true for Joe Rogan as well, at least among men without male authority figures in their lives. A month after the former Fear Factor host inked a more than $200 million multi-year contract extension with Spotify for the Joe Rogan Experience, a just released report says Rogan is the most trusted figure in media by almost half the men surveyed. In the fractured media environment of 2026, a stunning 49% of men to be exact. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Skydance Buyouts Impact CBS Stations; Local Chicago Anchor Among Those Departing News FCC To Vote On Plan To Relax Local TV And Radio Ownership Limits Adding to the texture of that result is a deeper dive that one-time MAGA kingmaker Rogan is considered the Walter Cronkite of our age by 41% of Democrats in the Beyond The Manosphere study from Precision Strategies and Tunnl Data. While Rogan tops the trust list, he is closely followed by Stephen A. Smith (38%) among the 3,001 men Precision, which was founded in 2015 by ex-Democratic operative and White House aide Stephanie Cutter, and Tunnl surveyed last month. Breaking down the pre-midterms data further, potential POTUS candidate and Donald Trump dining companion Smith is trailed as an info source by The Charlie Kirk Show , fellow ESPNer Pat McAfee, Ben Shapiro and ex-Fox News top dog Tucker Carlson . The dominance of conservative voices should be an alert to Democrats who are chest pounding over their big midterm elections wins, and how fragile that new coalition could be. At the same time, the pronounced shifts against buddy Trump that Rogan has articulated of late with slams against the stalemated Iran war that no one wants to be in” and the immigration abductions from “militarized police in the streets wearing masks.” Just over two years after endorsing Trump and six months after calling fights at the UFC Freedom 250 matches at the White House, Rogan a week ago seemed to be returning to his old stomping ground of being a Bernie Sanders fan. “They didn’t just lose the podcast bros,” the JRE host said on his November 13 podcast of the midterm rout of MAGA and the GOP. “They lost most of the country.” In testosterone territory, where video games are the primary community for the podcast bros, note the total Top 5 absence of traditional media like network and cable news anchors. They don’t exist. “Men and women share the same core of YouTube , Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok,” Sam Fitz, Precision’s SVP, Data & Analytics, tells Deadline. “YouTube is the center of gravity for both: 89% of men use it in a typical week, compared to 84% of women.” A national survey of 6,046 adults (3,001 men and 3,045 women), the 2026 report is also very telling on a number of levels of the Bowling Alone generation legacy and the so-called crisis among American males that has been assumed as an undercurrent to the populism and political upheaval of the last decade. Or, put another way, Joe Rogan is helping to heal Daddy issues. The latest look by Precision at the much-analyzed Manosphere spotlights that “nearly two-thirds of men (63%) say there is no man in their life they turn to for advice.” That Daddy or male authority figure deficit gets worse as income levels go down. The study from the integrated strategy and marketing agency states that “70% of men in households earning under $50,000 have no male mentor, as do 68% of rural men.” “This tells me that when asked directly, men seem to differentiate between who informs them and who guides them,” Precision’s Fitz notes of the male mentor gap the study reveals. “They have plenty of the former, and are sorely lacking when it comes to the latter. But that said, even if they don’t identify this themselves, it’s fair to assume that men without ‘mentors’ will fill the gap with Joe Rogan and other popular online content creators that talk through the issues men are dealing with.” Touching on topics of faith, race, money, marriage, family, the “emotional support” Millennial men get from chatbots (a lot!), culture and GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, the Manosphere study isn’t just about the fellas. In fact, looking at the data from the women surveyed may be one of the most telling aspects of the whole thing. While men seem to be more of media monolith with Team Rogan, women have far more and a greater diversity of trusted sources. Granted no single female trusted media source gets even half the pull of Rogan, the breakdown reflects the shift of the last decade ideologically and otherwise. (L-R) Kylie Kelce , Megyn Kelly , Candace Owens, Alex Cooper , Riley Gaines Getty Images To that, Not Gonna Lie podcast host Kylie Kelce is number #1 among women with the allegiance of 22% of those surveyed. Worth noting, self-declared left leaning Democrat Kelce has constantly given Rogan a run for his money and even beaten the UFC announcer in term of listeners and downloads since the September 2024 debut of Not Gonna Lie. After Kelce, who also appears in various other media with her spouse and ex-NFLer Jason Kelce, Megyn Kelly comes next for trusted source status among women. The rest of the Top 5 is filled out by conservative commentator Candace Owens, Call Her Daddy founder Alex Cooper, and former NCAA All-American and anti-trans activist Riley Gaines. With the right-ish preference of the men and women surveyed, a tendency to limit certain Constituational rights is also shined up in the Manosphere survey — one MAGA, DSA, Republicans, Democrats and Independents should pay serious attention to. In a landscape where faith in the government is lacking, “31% of men and 26% of women say the government should be able to limit press access for outlets it considers unfair or untruthful,” Precision’s SVP Fitz says of the study. “This jumps to about 50% for Republicans, men and women alike.” If all those lawsuits, credential revoking and “fake news” bluster is any indication, that last stat may be the Trump takeaway. title: Elizabeth Holmes’ Ex-Assistant Speaks Out on ‘You Can See Everything’ and Amanda Seyfried’s ‘Valid’ Performance: Holmes ‘Softened a Lot in the Film’
full_text: × Continue to Variety SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Nov 24, 2026 10:01am PT Elizabeth Holmes’ Ex-Assistant Speaks Out on ‘You Can See Everything’ and Amanda Seyfried’s ‘Valid’ Performance: Holmes ‘Softened a Lot in the Film’ By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest ‘Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’ Renewed for Season 4 at Amazon Prime Video 2 hours ago ‘SNL’ Sets Timothée Chalamet and Robert De Niro as Final Hosts of 2026 23 hours ago How Oobah Butler Scammed His Way to HBO 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images For Aria Marinelli, “ You Can See Everything ” hit a little close to home. Marinelli, who worked as Elizabeth Holmes ’ assistant in 2009, during the early stages of Theranos, spoke about watching her former boss in the documentary in an interview with Warner Bailey on “AvA Live.” “My initial reaction was I did not want to see it,” Marinelli said of the Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim film. But then, eventually, “I acquiesced and went out of sheer morbid curiosity, and I came out of there just feeling really contemplative. I mean, she’s a real human that I interacted with, and to see her up there going to jail with children was really emotionally charged for me, as someone who does have a kid as well.” Related Stories ‘PAW Patrol’ Spinoff Series ‘Skye’s Pup Squad’ Set for 2027 Release When “You Can See Everything” surprise premiered at Telluride and became one of the buzziest films of the year, Marinelli, who has rarely spoken about her time at Theranos 17 years ago, realized, “I have a voice in this too. [Holmes] doesn’t get to be the one to just come back on the scene and control the narrative.” Marinelli called the film a “crazy, wonderful, thoughtful, strategic piece,” and praised Fielder’s ability to portray Holmes as she truly is. “I do think he’s done it justice.” Compared to her time running the fraudulent blood-testing startup, “She seems like she’s softened a lot in the film,” Marinelli said of Holmes. “But she still seems like she really wants to win.” Courtesy of AvA Amanda Seyfried plays a big part in “You Can See Everything,” reprising her role as Holmes in reenactments with Fielder after the Theranos founder went to prison. One of the tension points in the three-hour A24 film is Seyfried’s portrayal of Holmes in the hit Hulu miniseries “The Dropout.” Billy Evans, Holmes’ romantic partner, clashes with Seyfried in the movie as he accuses her (and everyone else who worked on the series) of peddling lies about Holmes for the sake of entertainment. Marinelli, who knew Holmes intimately in 2009, said watching “The Dropout” was “remarkable” because “I can vouch for a lot of that.” (As an example: “I remember she listened to rap music really loud.”) Asked if she thought Seyfried’s depiction of Holmes was “fair,” Marinelli said, “Yeah, I do, because a lot of the things I saw were measured and valid. Obviously they’re dramatized, because it needs to keep people’s interest. But there was nothing I saw that seemed out of sorts with what I knew to be true.” Holmes is currently serving a 10-year prison sentence and is expected to be released in 2030. In the film, she and Evans tell Fielder they are working on a new biotech startup, continuing the progress of Theranos. As to whether Holmes deserves a second chance, Marinelli said, “I think people are complex, and we always deserve second chances. It might not be the best idea to go into the same field where you’ve already burned all the bridges, very publicly. It’s a complex question, and not for me to answer, because she needs to decide the direction her life takes after something like that. I can’t imagine what it must feel like to reset, especially if she truly believes she was following her dream. But yeah, I think we all deserve a second chance.” Bailey is the founder of Assistants vs. Agents, a digital media startup geared toward Hollywood’s labor class. On “AvA Live,” he interviews entertainment industry insiders and former assistants sharing advice for the next generation of leaders. Marinelli now works as the vice president of fan experience strategy at Arena One. Watch Marinelli’s full interview on “AvA Live” below. The streamer confirmed Tuesday that The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has been officially renewed for a fourth season. In addition, amid some online speculation, the company confirmed showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay will be back as well. The season is already in preproduction and will begin filming this spring at Shepperton Studios in the U.K. Related Stories TV 'The Rings of Power' Season 3 Trailer Is Full of Middle-earth Action, Simon Pegg Joins Cast TV 'The Rings of Power' Season 4 in Development, Eyes Filming in Early 2027 (Exclusive) “ The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has become a defining series for Prime Video,” said Peter Friedlander, head of global television at Amazon MGM Studios. “As season three delivers the landmark moment fans have been waiting for — the forging of the One Ring — we are proud to confirm season four with J.D. Payne, Patrick McKay and the entire creative team. We look forward to bringing fans even deeper into the rich world of Tolkien’s Second Age.” The news comes on the same day that the third season’s final two episodes will be available for streaming a day earlier than originally announced — tonight at 9 p.m. Eastern on Prime Video. According to Prime Video, season three launched two weeks ago and has reached 33 million viewers worldwide through its first 12 days following its Nov. 11 premiere and it ranks among Prime Video’s Top 10 most-watched returning seasons ever. Official Nielsen ratings for the season’s debut week aren’t out yet, however. According to Rotten Tomatoes, the show’s critics’ scores were steady with past seasons (averaging around 85 percent “Fresh”). The show’s audience scores continued to be underwater, but the show has been a controversial one among LOTR fans for various reasons from the outset and getting an accurate sense of the show’s reception can be tricky. title: Music Streamer Tidal Targets AI-Generated Tracks, Saying They Will Be “Rejected And Removed” Starting Next Month
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Music Streamer Tidal Targets AI-Generated Tracks, Saying They Will Be “Rejected And Removed” Starting Next Month ‘Caréme’ & ‘División Palermo’ Take Top Prizes At International Emmy Awards: Full Winners List David Zaslav Recalls “Awkward Moment” Before Skydance Merger Close, Hails Ex-WBD Global Chief Gerhard Zeiler For Keeping Staff “Motivated” View All November 24, 2026 9:55am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Tidal , a formerly artist-backed music streamer once controlled by Jack Dorsey’s Block, is taking an aggressive stand against AI . Citing a massive surge of artificially created music, the company on Tuesday announced a complete ban taking effect on December 9. As of that date, the company said in a post on X that any wholly AI track detected on the platform will be “rejected and removed.” In the past 90 days, the company says, 43% of all tracks on its platform have been detected as wholly AI-generated. Tidal labeled them (a step many other companies have also been taking) and removed them from its royalty pool. On November 6, the company added, “we had the greatest influx of AI music yet: Over 60% of the deliveries we received were wholly AI generated.” Related Stories News Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang As CEO News CAA's Bryan Lourd Urges Congress To Pass AI Legislation To Protect Americans "Famous Or Not" As of now, Tidal estimates that 27 million tracks (about 6% of the total in its catalog) are tagged as AI. But they are a zombie-like presence, with 96% of the titles receiving zero streams over the past 90 days. Watch on Deadline “Wholly AI-generated music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists is another serious problem that has only increased in scale: It diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans,” the company wrote. “To date, we’ve taken down over 65,000 tracks flagged for suspected artist-name impersonation. “It’s true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fanbases. title: ‘Hexed’ Review: Disney’s Bewitching Animation Is A Surprisingly Edgy Y.A. Fantasy
full_text: Skip to main content By Damon Wise Damon Wise Film Editor, Awards yo_damo More Stories By Damon ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Review: Is Time Finally Running Out For The Dystopic Game Show Franchise? ‘How To Rob A Bank’ Review: Crony Capitalism Gets Blowback In David Leitch’s Anarchic Heist Tutorial ‘7 Miles Out’ Review: Carol Morley’s Coming-Of-Age Drama Channels The Rebellious Spirit Of ’70s Youth View All November 24, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source ‘Hexed’ © 2026 Disney Enterprises “Have you ever been persecuted, drowned or burned at the stake?” Conditions for entry to the city of Hexe are pretty rigorous and surprisingly dark in this engaging Disney animation. After playing things safe with 2023’s almost immediately forgettable, formulaic Wish , the studio has somehow turned the tanker round with a surprisingly edgy Y.A. fantasy that sometimes seems in danger of going too far in the opposite direction. Mention of warlocks in the stylish prologue is a little misleading; Hexed is a film about witches all the way, a hectic but mostly very entertaining fantasy that seems curiously beholden to Wicked , in ways that threaten to seriously undermine everything that’s good about it. Related Stories Casting Hailee Steinfeld Confirms She's In 'Avengers: Doomsday' News How Jodie Foster Took Her First Disney Voice Role In 'Hexed' And Lent Her Smile To Her Character - Contenders L.A. Girl power is the central theme, introducing Billie Doe ( Hailee Steinfeld ) as an Ohio infant with special powers, whose mother Alice ( Rashida Jones ) watches over her with a cautious eye after almost losing her to a couple of crows that once appeared through a portal to another world. Fast-forward a few years, and Billie is now going through her difficult teenage years, borrowing her mother’s car without permission (or a licence) to set the school mascot — significantly, an owl — free into the wild. The headmaster is on the warpath, but, while hiding in the bathroom, Billie manifests a strange ability to move things with her mind. Watch on Deadline Billie’s supernatural talents are somehow connected to a bracelet she has been forced to wear since childhood, and after she takes it off for a second time, the portal returns and sucks her into a parallel dimension. After being inducted by a talking book and a pen (Stephen Fry and Tracey Ullman respectively), Billie becomes a citizen of Hexe, a sanctuary city for practitioners of the occult. Hexe, though, is not quite the land of the free that it first appears to be; under the reign of Queen Celeste ( Jodie Foster ), it is very much a two-tier society, divided into those who indulge its narcissistic ruler and those who don’t. For reasons that seem fairly obvious already, Alice follows her daughter to Hexe and tries to send her home in an enchanted cauldron while she distracts the local police chief. Instead, however, Billie follows the cryptic label on a magic potion that leads her to Beef Roger Crummchuk ( Walton Goggins ), a three-eyed cat and one-time familiar to Queen Celeste’s daughter. After an extended sequence in which Billie begs for his help — lots of scenes gone on far too long — Beef Roger decides to help Billie look for Alice, who is now locked up behind barred doors and windows in a tower at the royal palace. Comparisons with Wicked were always going to be inevitable, but the extent to which Hexed leans into them goes way beyond homage, notably in Queen Celeste’s fleet of flying bird-women with creepy fluorescent eyes. Hexe itself even looks like Emerald City, and when Billie first embarks on her adventure, she tells Beef Roger that “We’re gonna yellow-brick-road it”, the only time The Wizard of Oz is consciously mentioned. And once again, the climax involves the unmasking of an impostor, as Queen Celeste manipulates the talents of others to perform a centuries-old moon spell and gain ultimate power. There’s still a lot to like, however, especially in its use of witchcraft as a metaphor; much play is made of Billie’s teenage-emo awkwardness, with her purple hair, spindly legs and clunky goth boots (“You think there’s something wrong with me,” she wails to her long-suffering mother). Surprisingly, there is no father in the picture, and the story boils down to an interesting three-way dynamic between Alice, her daughter and the Queen, one that doesn’t quite take the direction you might be expecting. A great and very eclectic voice cast helps in this regard, with Goggins a surprisingly calming presence whenever things get hectic (and they do). But while Foster’s frosty Queen Celeste offers a refreshing return to the unreconstructed Disney villainesses of old, the rest of Hexed can’t help but seem retrofitted to get us there. There are welcome shades of Zootopia in its world-building — notably a town of familiars, and a rowdy pirate bar — but the story takes some strange turns, especially when, as Queen Celeste’s plan is about to unfold, we go back, albeit briefly, to Ohio. Its message — the usual be-yourself, do-your-thing — is harmless enough, mind. It’s just disappointing that a film so high on intention, ignition and inwitchification should fall so short in the inspiration department. There’s still enough potential for a sequel, mind. title: the chorus of grief
full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic “Not True”: Antoine Fuqua Alleged Gun Assault Of Bar Manager Over Daughter Rebuked By Reps Indie Film Accountant Gets Prison For Stealing Millions For Sugar Daddy Hook-Ups, Vegas Visits & Louis Vuitton Gear Palisades Fire Arson Suspect Convicted, Faces 40 Years In Prison View All August 25, 2026 8:14pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Taylor Swift and Dolly Parton Getty Images “A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right,” Taylor Swift said tonight of her friend Dolly Parton . The beloved country music legend died Tuesday at the age of 80 , following a “brief battle with cancer,” according to her reps . “But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one,” the Life of a Showgirl superstar said of multi-Grammy winner, Oscar nominee and Dollywood founder. Swift has long be an open admirer of the trailblazing Parton. The appreciation was mutual. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Sports Imax To Screen Super Bowl In Deal With Disney, NFL Obituaries Tom Jackson Dies: Broncos Alum & ESPN Hall Of Fame Broadcaster Was 75 As recently as earlyJuly, Parton put out a video thank you to Swift and then soon-to-be hubby Travis Kelce for including a $2 million donation to the Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library. On the eve of their media frenzied MSG wedding, which Parton was invited to but did not attend, Swift and the NFL vet gave millions to 20 charities across the nation. Today, as America and the world lamented the death of the ‘Jolene’ performer , 9 To 5 actor, producer, playwright, philanthropist, and author, Swift offered personal words of grief and joy. The ‘Cruel Summer’ singer said of Tennessee native Parton: “She was truly the gift that kept on giving. Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. Somehow she was able to give us her lessons about the world gently and honestly, simultaneously, and oftentimes hilariously. She managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted. Somehow she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist. Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it. For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too. Dolly, I’ll think of you each step of the way.” Amen.
